paper: LLM-Powered Multi-Agent System for Automated Crypto Portfolio Management
source_url: first-author repository pinned in the MACI source audit
version_scope: v1/v2 four-expert GPT-4o experiment; v3 is a materially different 2025 experiment and is not substituted
headline_strategy: Four-expert crypto allocation system using fine-tuned GPT-4o agents for cross-sectional coin/image analysis and market/news analysis, combining weekly expert probabilities over the CoinGecko top-30 universe into top-quintile, linear-probability, and market-weighted portfolios

paper_configuration.test_lineage: November 2023 through September 2024 stated; figures/source conflict on endpoint

paper_portability_to_common_task: not defensibly executable because the trained expert checkpoints, inference records, market inputs, weekly universes and result portfolios are absent, and the method is crypto-specific
missing_headline_objects: the actual uploaded fine-tuning file ID, job ID, active selected checkpoint, and paper-run linkage
paper-time coin prices, blockchain factors, market/news records, processed inputs, and weekly top-30 memberships
immutable inference requests/responses, predictions, token/logprob records, retries, and API-cost ledger
released expert checkpoint pickles and prediction JSON records required by the runner
paper portfolio arrays, holdings, costs/slippage, and result tables
a source-defined transfer from crypto/blockchain/image inputs to monthly U.S. stock characteristics
source_conflicts: The raw pre-submission source fails its declared Python 3.9 contract and omits a gitignored constants module.
Only one single-agent fine-tuning call is active; multi-agent expert blocks are commented.
The same fine-tuned agent object is serialized under both cross-sectional-vision and market-news checkpoint names.
Recovered 962-message payloads and 930 images were added after paper v2, so they do not prove paper-upload identity.
The test endpoint differs among paper prose, figures, and source handlers.

rejected_substitutes.route: Fine-tune a new GPT-4o or accessible vision model on the recovered payload
rejected_substitutes.reason: The recovered training package postdates v2, the actual paper job/checkpoint is unverified, and a new remote training run would produce a different policy.

rejected_substitutes.route: Run the source with researcher-inferred constants and synthetic blockchain data
rejected_substitutes.reason: The existing overlay reaches component checks only and stops at missing blockchain inputs; synthetic values cannot generate the paper policy.

rejected_substitutes.route: Use the released top-quintile/linear/market portfolio functions with arbitrary scores
rejected_substitutes.reason: These rules consume missing expert predictions; arbitrary scores would not be MACI decisions.
V3 changes the architectures, capabilities, model families, calendar and experimental lineage under the same arXiv identifier.

rejected_substitutes.route: Map crypto experts to JKP stock factors
rejected_substitutes.reason: No source mapping exists from blockchain/coin images/news and weekly top-30 crypto selection to monthly U.S. stocks.

result_policy: No new fine-tune, synthetic-data overlay, arbitrary-score portfolio, v3 strategy, or generic JKP mapping is entered as a v1/v2 MACI return. Its positive crypto results remain unresolved rather than classified as false or as JKP underperformance.
